stem: A child aged 1 to 8 years is using Flixotide Junior but now needs a dose higher than 100 micrograms twice daily; what is the most appropriate next formulation step?

options.text: Replace preventer therapy with nightly oxygen
Use oral prednisone as the regular preventer
Stop inhaled therapy until the next flare-up

explanation: Switch to Flixotide. When a child aged 1 to 8 years needs more than 100 micrograms twice daily of Flixotide Junior, the next formulation step is to switch to Flixotide.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the formulation should change when the dose requirement exceeds 100 micrograms twice daily.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because children aged 1 to 8 years using Flixotide Junior who need a higher dose than 100 micrograms twice daily should switch to Flixotide.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because nightly oxygen is not a long-term preventer formulation step.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because oral prednisone is not the regular inhaled preventer therapy for this situation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because inhaled preventer therapy should not be stopped when ongoing asthma control is still needed.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
